Marta: Quick kickoff for the reserved-pools/occupancy-bands discussion. We need a concise decision for Q2 planning: do we ship occupancy bands (soft overcommit tiers per pool) + automatic fallback to burst pools, or keep simple hard quotas for launch?

Alex: TL;DR — occupancy bands give better utilization but add complexity to scheduling and billing. Need clear SLOs and a rollout plan.

Ben: Agree with Alex. Customers that asked (FinReg and SearchCo) want predictable latency under peak. Hard quotas easier to promise.

Sophia: From runtime POV, occupancy bands look like this: "green" (<=60% GPU utilization) no throttling, "amber" (60-85%) delayed queueing + soft preemption, "red" (>85%) route to burst or degrade quality. We can implement with existing eviction tokens.

Marta: Concrete tradeoffs:
- Predictability: hard quotas win
- Unit cost: bands win (higher utilization)
- Ops complexity: bands + fallback win because more moving parts
- Customer trust: depends on observability + fail-open guarantees (fallback to burst)

Jenny: Ops question — if we do bands + fallback, what are the telemetry and alerts? We need token-level billing mapping for amber/red transitions, and an SLA escalation path.

Alex: Proposed minimal telemetry for launch: per-pool occupancy time-series, per-tenant fallback count, median p95 latency during amber/red, and number of preemptions. We can add a rollout gate: must have spike-sim tests + 2 pilot customers.

Ben: Pilot customers: FinReg (compliance workloads) and MediaCo (spiky embeddings). Both willing but FinReg requires audit logs and opt-out of preemption.

Sophia: Implementation outline (runtime):
```
- Add occupancy tracker per GPU pool (rolling 1m/5m window)
- Annotate requests with priority bands
- Scheduler: if pool in amber -> allow new low-priority requests to join queue for up to 150ms before routing to burst
- If red -> immediate routing for low-priority; high-priority pinned or rejected based on customer opt-in
```

Alex: That queueing delay number is tunable. For launch I recommend conservative defaults: amber delay=100ms, burst-routing threshold=82% occupancy.

Marta: Pricing & billing implications? We can't surprise customers. Proposal: show occupancy band in Console + include fallback events in invoice line-item (count of routed tokens to burst).

Ben: Billing owners push back on per-event charges for pilot customers. Suggest: first 90 days in pilot -> waived burst surcharge, but we ship telemetry + invoice preview.

Jenny: Ops runbook additions:
- Alert: pool occupancy > 85% for 5m -> paging (oncall)
- Playbook: if high fallback rate, throttle new signups to pool and open incident bridge
- Expiry: automated scaling down not allowed during pilot windows

Marta: Launch criteria checklist I'm proposing:
1) Spike-sim with 2x expected peak and no >2x p95 latency regression
2) Feature flags for bands + fallback wired to Console toggles
3) Pilot with 2 customers for 6 weeks + billing preview
4) Observability: dashboards + alerting + invoice line item visible
5) Rollout plan: % of tenants in next 2 sprints (10% -> 30% -> 100%)

Alex: One important scope negotiation item: do we support per-tenant custom band thresholds at launch? That's more product work. I'd say no for MVP — global per-pool thresholds only.

Ben: +1 to global thresholds. Add a customer escape hatch: opt-out to hard quota mode (if they need absolute predictability).

Sophia: Runtime knobs for future: per-model priority, per-tenant reserved slots, fast-fail policy for low-latency classes. We'll record these as backlog items.

Marta: Action items:
- Alex: write spike-sim scenario and target SLOs (due Tue)
- Sophia: prototype occupancy tracker + amber queue (demo Fri)
- Jenny: draft ops playbook + billing lines (due Wed)
- Ben: coordinate pilot commitments and legal opt-out for FinReg (due next Tue)

Alex: Noted. Also recommending a small safety throttle: global soft-cap on number of concurrent fallbacks to burst to avoid surge costs.

Jenny: Thoughts on customer communication: we should pre-announce as "Reserved Pools Beta: occupancy bands and automatic fallback" with clear docs and console indicators + opt-out.

Ben: Legal asks: for FinReg, pre-approval of audit logs and a clause for no surprise billing. I'll loop in legal.

Marta: Ok team — decision summary for planning: ship MVP with occupancy bands (global thresholds) + automatic fallback, pilot customers with waived surge fees for 90 days, hard quota opt-out for customers who require it. If any objections please flag by EOD.

Sophia: No objections on my side.

Alex: Fine by me, as long as spike-sim and rollout gates are enforced.

Jenny: 👍 I'll start the ops doc and alert templates.

eng-bot: Deployed feature-flag scaffold to staging: ff/reserved-pools/occupancy-bands (enabled for alpha orgs).

Marta: Thanks — closing thread. We'll sync next Tues to review prototypes.
